inlet_reference.name: Cold normal-shock diffuser reference
inlet_reference.scope: Area continuity and ideal station states only. Not a scramjet inlet, installed inlet design, or solved RBCC/TBCC cycle.
assumptions: Full capture; no spillage, bleed, friction or boundary-layer displacement.
Normal shock at the inlet plane; constant gamma=1.4 and R=286.9 J/(kg K).
Exit Mach is the lesser of 0.3 and 80% of post-shock Mach.
Length, aspect ratio and wall thickness are geometry inputs, not aerodynamic optimizations.

sizing.gradation_scope: Target size slope; actual cell growth is audited separately in volume meshes.

tessellation.scope: CAD boundary triangulation; solver volumes have separate quality reports.

equations: Tt/T = 1 + (gamma−1)M²/2
pt/p = (Tt/T)^(gamma/(gamma−1))
Mass flow = density × speed × area
Net thrust = exit mass flow × exit speed − capture mass flow × flight speed + pressure thrust (not evaluated)

assumptions: Perfect-gas mixture with mass-weighted cp and R.
Declared air/fuel ratio and combustion efficiency.
Steady one-dimensional common nozzle with ideal supersonic expansion.
Mixer and combustor pressure losses are bounded inputs pending reacting CFD.
unresolved: Boundary-layer separation, unstart and three-dimensional mixing

inverse_sizing.scope: Conditional inverse rocket equation with fixed tank radii, wall thickness, materials and all non-tank masses. It does not resize the enclosing assembly, predict flight losses, or qualify a single-stage vehicle.

mass_budget.scope: Gross component mass estimate with explicit equipment allowance and margin. Orbital array, battery and radiator masses use declared sizing assumptions. Uncut core envelopes overcount some material; cooling ports, core ribs/jacket, pressurant bottle, valves, vehicle skin, payload bay, wings, power distribution hardware, avionics and TPS are not independently modeled. Overlaps are not unioned. No upper/lower mass bound or manufactured material assignment is claimed.

orbital_resources.scope: Circular Earth orbit, zero-beta central eclipse, normal solar incidence and constant load. No orbit lifetime, attitude solution, transient temperatures, surface view factors, solar/albedo heating, array pointing/deployment, peak loads, battery cycling qualification, power distribution hardware, atmospheric heating or reentry model. Radiator uses one isothermal emitting face and a user-assumed effective sink. Areal masses and battery performance are assumptions, not selected hardware.

stages.title: Requirements and domain checks
equations: range checks; architecture and model-domain gates
assumptions: User-entered requirements define a single operating point.

checks.name: all inputs finite and within declared bounds

stages.title: Propellant and chamber state
equations: NASA CEA equilibrium state via RocketCEA; R = R_universal / molecular_weight
assumptions: Equilibrium chamber properties; downstream frozen constant-property approximation.

checks.name: source and finite positive gas properties

stages.title: Ideal choked nozzle solution
equations: A/A* = area_ratio(M,gamma)
F = mdot Ve + (pe - pa) Ae
mdot = A* Pc/sqrt(Tc) sqrt(gamma/R) (2/(gamma+1))^((gamma+1)/(2(gamma-1)))
assumptions: Steady, one-dimensional, attached, isentropic flow; constant gamma and gas constant.

stages.title: Shared pressure-wall and cooling-route recipe
equations: solved throat/exit area -> shared axial profile
profile + passage sizing inputs -> cooling centerlines
assumptions: Contours and channel centerlines are parametric geometry; hot gas loads are not solved.

stages.title: Pressure-fed mass and pressure network
equations: mdot_total = mdot_fuel + mdot_oxidizer
Delta p = f (L/D) rho V^2/2; p_tank >= p_chamber + losses + reserve
V_tank = mdot t_burn / (rho (1 - ullage))
assumptions: Steady, incompressible, single-phase branches; Darcy friction and nominal properties.
Equilibrium chamber chemistry coupled to steady hydraulics; constant-property ideal nozzle and liquids. No combustion kinetics, stability, or regulation prediction.

ideal mixer mass and enthalpy balance
compressible station mass-flow relation

stages.title: Orbital power, eclipse energy and radiator sizing
equations: T_orbit = 2*pi*sqrt(r^3/mu); eclipse fraction = asin(R_earth/r)/pi
sunlight array energy = full-orbit load energy + battery conversion losses
Q_radiator = epsilon*sigma*A*(T_radiator^4 - T_sink^4)
array/radiator mass = area * assumed areal mass; battery mass = nominal Wh / assumed Wh/kg
assumptions: Circular Earth orbit, zero-beta central eclipse, normal solar incidence and constant load. No orbit lifetime, attitude solution, transient temperatures, surface view factors, solar/albedo heating, array pointing/deployment, peak loads, battery cycling qualification, power distribution hardware, atmospheric heating or reentry model. Radiator uses one isothermal emitting face and a user-assumed effective sink. Areal masses and battery performance are assumptions, not selected hardware.

validation.statement: Verification checks implementation consistency. Physical validation requires matched test measurements.

limits: Airbreathing installed performance, unstart and mode-transition operability
Vehicle mass closure, coupled ascent, reentry and thermal protection
Injector atomization, finite-rate mixing and combustion stability
Regulator and valve hardware, cavitation and real-gas transients
Conjugate heat transfer, boiling and verified wall temperature
Tank end caps, joints, fatigue and proof testing

obligations.required_output: Closed subsystem mass budget and collision-checked payload/vehicle packaging
Coupled ascent and orbital insertion meeting the mission with declared margins
Vehicle loads, stress, buckling, joints and fatigue closure
Vehicle thermal balance and applicable ascent/reentry protection
Power/energy, guidance/navigation/control, communications and attitude-control budgets
Process-specific tolerances, inspection access and matched physical evidence
Airbreathing net thrust, fuel staging and mode-transition operating envelope

system_completion.statement: Passing equation residuals and mesh checks establishes software consistency, not whole-spacecraft engineering closure.
